newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Gunman surrenders after Swiss church siege.
newsitem.headline: Gunman surrenders after Swiss church siege.

text.p: A gunman who shot and wounded two people surrendered to Swiss police early on Sunday after holing up for six hours in a Geneva church, police said.
"He has surrendered. He has been arrested," said a police spokesman.
The gunman opened fire in the Notre Dame Roman Catholic church shortly after evening mass ended at 7.30 p.m. (1830 GMT), wounding a priest and a sexton in the legs.
Armed police sealed off the city centre church and brought in psychologists to try to calm the man down. The gunman, whose motives remained unclear, demanded to see the city's police chiefs.
Police said he made a series of calls with a mobile phone. The man was believed to be a lawyer and former Swiss army officer.
